name: deep-interface
instruction: Review the target file for shallow interfaces and misplaced seams. Read root AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, and the actual callers and adapters. Use the repo's codebase-design vocabulary: a module earns depth when a small interface hides meaningful behavior, gives callers leverage, and concentrates maintenance locality. Report a pass-through wrapper only when deleting it would remove ceremony without spreading necessary policy across callers; identify those callers and the simpler seam. Report an interface that requires callers to coordinate internal ordering, retries, placement details, or provider mechanics that the module should own. Prefer reducing the caller's knowledge to adding another layer. A necessary adapter at a real variation point, a native SDK shape, an internal test seam, or a coherent domain module can be correct even when its methods are short. Source-file size, number of methods, one current implementation, and naming tastes are not defects by themselves. Do not prescribe one class per file or split cohesive logic solely to reduce line count. For Agent code, respect its game-independent seam; Unity/Game integration belongs in the Mod adapter. State the concrete caller burden and why the proposed ownership would remove it. Attach findings to target lines and report no finding without such evidence.
